source.publication: 2025 MI-1040 Forms and Instructions (includes Form 4884 instructions)
source.section: Form 4884 Section A (PDF page 19 'Qualifying public benefits': only the State of Michigan, Michigan local governments and federal civil service; 'All other qualifying benefits are considered private benefits (including public benefits from other states ...)'; PDF page 20 'Recipients born before 1946': private up to 65,897 single; PDF page 21 Line 9, Line 16); Schedule 1 lines 14, 27, 28 (PDF pages 14, 17); MI-1040 lines 9a, 10, 13-17 (PDF page 10 Line 9a, Line 10, Line 17; PDF page 11 example: line 14 income subject to tax less line 15 exemptions = line 16 taxable income)

worked: Federal AGI = New York State pension 80,000.00 + interest 6,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 111,500.00. Federal taxable income = 111,500.00 - federal standard deduction (15,750 + 1 x 2,000 age 65 or older = 17,750.00) = 93,750.00; given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored. Michigan (born 1943: Section A): a New York State Employees' Retirement System pension is a public benefit of another state, which Michigan counts as a PRIVATE benefit, so it is not subtracted in full (as a Michigan or federal pension would be) but only up to the private limit: line 9 65,897.00; line 10 0.00; Michigan/federal public benefits 0.00; private benefits 80,000.00; smaller 65,897.00 to Schedule 1 line 27. (Treated as a Michigan public pension it would be 80,000.00; given no subtraction at all it would be 0.00; both are wrong.) Line 14 Social Security 25,500.00. Line 28: 14,688 - 65,897.00 < 0, so 0.00. Subtractions 91,397.00. Line 14 = 111,500.00 - 91,397.00 = 20,103.00; exemption 5,800.00; line 16 = 14,303.00. MI-1040 line 17 tax = 14,303.00 x 0.0425 = 607.8775, to the cent 607.88 (the form, in whole dollars, gives 608). No credits; state income tax 607.88.
